key_insight: ClinDataBench shows that LLM agents can construct clinical trial analysis datasets, but fewer validator findings do not guarantee correct data derivations.
clinical_relevance: This work could support more reliable preparation of regulatory trial evidence; it does not evaluate cancer treatments or discover new drugs.
method: Agents transform 22 public CDISC pilot study domains, an analysis plan and specifications into 13 ADaM datasets, Define-XML metadata and offline rebuild code.
A host-only evaluator separately measures standards conformance, selected derivations, reproducibility and effort.
Compare initial submissions, self-refinement and revision using agents’ own validator reports.
evidence_signal: In an exploratory six-model pilot, all four CRITIC workflows with usable validator comparisons reduced findings, but none reduced failed derivations.
watch_item: Structural validation cannot establish analytical correctness: the package with the fewest findings lacked all 234 efficacy summary records in the specified form.
paper_title: ClinDataBench: Benchmarking Large Language Model Agents in Clinical Trial Analysis Dataset Construction
